subject.title: feat(fleet): multi-tenant hosting via openclaw fleet cell supervisor

question: Should OpenClaw core own the experimental Fleet supervisor after its persistence, networking, allocation, merge-conflict, and proof blockers are corrected?
rationale: Even a corrected patch creates a long-lived privileged host lifecycle and tenant-isolation contract, so implementation correctness alone cannot determine product and security ownership.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core feature
options.body: Rebuild on current main, resolve all blockers, and accept the experimental lifecycle contract after Linux security and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep orchestration external
options.body: Define a supported cell contract while a separately maintained operator project owns Fleet lifecycle and host administration.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Defer the feature until maintainers are ready to own its threat model, support burden, and compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core feature
recommendation.body: Rebuild on current main, resolve all blockers, and accept the experimental lifecycle contract after Linux security and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle owns the linked design, all Fleet commits, and adjacent Docker and Codex contracts in current history.
